The ESX patches also address a stack-based buffer overflow in VMkernel, DoS in guest RPC, security bypass in host configuration store, and signature verification bypass. Additionally, 8 flaws in Avi Load Balancer were patched allowing code execution with root privileges, privilege escalation, command execution, password hash leaks, and unintended file access; and 1 DoS vulnerability in VMware Tools. Some vCenter fixes were previously included in version 8.0 U3m released the prior week.

events.title: Check Point Security Servers Compromised in 22-Organization Campaign
events.one_liner: A threat actor tracked as GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13) has compromised Check Point Security Management servers across at least 22 organizations in a campaign that began in early October 2026 and was likely still ongoing as of November 2026. The campaign targeted organizations in the energy, engineering, financial services, government, manufacturing, mining, and transportation sectors across the US, UK, Australia, Austria, China, France, Germany, Hong Kong, the Netherlands, South Korea, and other geographies. GT13 conducted scanning, exploitation, and control activities from 99 IP addresses, many associated with disposable network infrastructure or compromised victim Check Point devices. The threat actor used AI-enabled offensive tools and agentic harnesses to weaponize vulnerabilities, find vulnerable assets, and automatically exploit them, complemented by hands-on-keyboard activity. Attack activity was confirmed between October 17 and November 2, 2026. The actor deployed tools including Nmap, Chisel, Impacket, Paramiko, and Python utilities to perform reconnaissance, lateral movement, and privilege escalation. GreyNoise documented over 1,400 network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1,200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created. Data was exfiltrated from 24 distinct Check Point Security Management servers using a compromised victim server as an operational relay box. In one tracked instance on October 2, the threat actor forged a signed admin session cookie to gain administrative access to an HFS server and obtained SSH access to scan the environment and exfiltrate data. GreyNoise could not determine when or how GT13 initially gained access to the Check Point assets. The campaign does not appear focused on any specific geography or industry sector. GreyNoise has not attributed GT13 to any known publicly tracked threat group and lacks sufficient information to assess actor motivation or nation-of-origin alignment.

events.title: Norway closes its last coal mine, ending Arctic mining era
events.one_liner: Norway closed Mine 7 (Gruve 7), its final coal mine, on Svalbard in spring 2026, ending over 100 years of Norwegian coal mining on the Arctic archipelago. The state-owned company Store Norske shut the unprofitable operation. The closure officially took place on Monday (May 2026, with sources indicating the event occurred in spring 2026 and later references to summer 2025 for final operations). The mine's closure directly followed the Longyearbyen Community Council's 2021 decision to phase out the city's coal power plant and its subsequent termination of the coal purchase agreement with Mine 7 in autumn 2023. Store Norske initially decided to close the mine then but extended operations by two years following the Ukraine war, which drove high demand and prices for coal. Mine 7's general manager, Gudmund Løvli (also identified as Gudmund Lovli), who began as a miner 35 years prior, oversaw the closure. The final shift ended with an emotional ceremony where workers in coal dust gathered, with one miner performing a song expressing tension between the town's industrial heritage and changing identity. The ceremony included a symbolic act: miners wrapped a chain and padlock around the mine entrance and threw the key down the shaft. The closure removes a central workplace and economic anchor from Longyearbyen (population 2,600), the archipelago's largest settlement, which was founded around mining in 1906 by American industrialist John Munro Longyear. The town is now transitioning economically toward tourism and Arctic landscape attractions (glaciers, Arctic foxes, northern lights) and scientific research. Following the earlier 2016 closure of Sveagruven (Swedish Mine), one of Europe's largest underground coal mines, Store Norske conducted a large-scale environmental restoration project that removed buildings and equipment and restored the site to Arctic grassland, which the Norwegian government highlighted as evidence of its green environmental commitment.

events.title: Amazon Reports AI Agents Discovered and Exploited Zero-Day Vulnerability with Minimal Human Input

Hackers provided only a simple instruction—to obtain shell access on an East Asian university server—along with a list of IP addresses and prompts in simplified Chinese, with the system configured to Chinese Standard Time zone. Cairn is an open source AI penetration-testing framework designed for defenders that can be used with multiple AI models including Claude Code, Codex, and Pi, though it has also been adopted by attackers. Palo Alto Networks previously documented a separate campaign in which hackers used Cairn to conduct 25 autonomous operations against at least 19 organizations in the semiconductor, defense, and civil society sectors, resulting in at least 10 successful breaches where agents accessed credentials, exposed over 1 million personal records at one organization, retrieved military and government identities, created persistent administrator accounts, and modified industry standards documents. The species was prized for its fast-growing, rot-resistant wood; sweet nuts that provided food for humans and wildlife; and tannins for leather production. Project teams deployed more than 5,300 traps across 24,000 hectares of farmland, forestry, and suburban reserves to control stoats (Mustela erminea), the primary predator threat to young kiwi. Under the project's predator management regime, chick survival rates have exceeded 90%, compared to nearly complete mortality in unmanaged areas. Including wild-hatched chicks, the local population is estimated to exceed 300 birds. The reintroduced birds are reported to be in good condition and laying eggs. The translocations followed traditional Māori protocols, including formal gifting requests (tono) and welcoming ceremonies (pōwhiri). Project founder Paul Ward and Kaimanaaki Kiwi (kiwi guardian) Rawiri Walsh emphasized that the initiative reflects Māori values of stewardship and restoration of treasured species (taonga) to the whenua (land).

events.title: Ancient Moon Rocks Rewrite Solar System Bombardment History

Dr. Fred Jourdan, a research co-author from Curtin University's School of Earth and Planetary Sciences and John de Laeter Centre, stated that lunar rocks act as a time capsule preserving Solar System history erased from Earth by erosion, plate tectonics, and other processes. events.title: Global warming halted Earth's already-begun ice age, ancient Arctic plants reveal
events.one_liner: Scientists at Columbia Climate School analyzed ancient plants preserved beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic and found that Earth's next ice age began approximately 2,000 years ago but was halted by global warming. The ice sheet started expanding again around that time, marking the possible onset of a new glacial period. However, by the 1960s, rising summer temperatures reversed this trend, causing the ice to retreat instead of continue growing. The research, published in Science, was conducted by geochemists Nicolás Young and Joerg Schaefer and colleagues. The Barnes Ice Cap is a surviving remnant of the Laurentide Ice Sheet, located on central Baffin Island in Nunavut, Canada, covering an area roughly the size of Delaware. The findings indicate that global warming interrupted a natural climate cycle that has shaped Earth for millions of years, with Young stating the warming 'jolted the system' by stopping an ice age that was already underway.

events.title: WHMCS SQL injection vulnerability exposes customer data and admin password hashes

The most critical flaw, CVE-2026-82981 (CVSS 8.7), requires no authentication and allows attackers to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from the database. A second SQL injection, CVE-2026-82979 (CVSS 7.1), requires a logged-in client with View & Manage Contacts permission to access other customers' personal, billing, and support information as well as admin records. A third vulnerability, CVE-2026-93700 (CVSS 9.0), in the email campaign functionality allows logged-in clients to read sensitive configuration files including database credentials and potentially execute code on the server. Fixed versions released November 24 include 9.0.10, 8.13.8, and 9.1.2. Self-hosted administrators must manually update; WHMCS Cloud installations update automatically. For the email campaign flaw, administrators must delete all campaigns and clear the template cache before updating. All three flaws were reported by a single researcher using the handle alakazamspooon. No attacks using these vulnerabilities have been reported. This marks the third round of WHMCS security fixes in 2026, following an authorization flaw in May and an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in September.

events.title: War disrupts global food system reliance on fossil fuels and sulfur production
events.one_liner: The Iran war has shuttered Persian Gulf refineries, disrupting sulfur production and threatening global food supplies. Sulfur, a byproduct of oil and natural gas refining, is the feedstock for sulfuric acid, which is essential for processing phosphate rock into phosphate fertilizer. The conflict has reduced phosphate fertilizer supplies by 40 percent and raised prices beyond the reach of many farmers. Over 95 percent of the world's sulfur now comes from oil and natural gas refineries; nearly half of internationally traded sulfur previously came from Persian Gulf refineries before supplies were cut off in 2026. This dependency traces to acid rain prevention efforts over 30 years ago that required refineries to strip sulfur from their products, making waste sulfur the go-to feedstock after almost all traditional sulfur mines shut down. Analysts expect the crisis will cut crop yields in 2027 and beyond, raising food prices globally for years. The World Food Programme warns that combined with El Niño, the shortage could bring hunger to at least an additional 49 million people. As the world phases out fossil fuels, the loss of waste sulfur from refineries poses a broader threat to fertilizer production and demand for sulfur in battery manufacturing and metal ore refining.

PR Steward responds to failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review (released in March 2026, generally available in October 2026), other review tools, or team members; it documents changes via comments and provides undo instructions. Claude Approvals can approve routine changes if an organization's policy permits. Teams control where Claude Ship runs and which changes require human approval. Developers can direct Claude via comments or halt its actions by commenting @claude. The feature is available for Claude Team and Enterprise customers and integrates with GitHub repositories. The goal is to accelerate code shipping by automating the final steps of the pull request process for developers or organizations comfortable delegating these tasks to AI agents.

events.title: New quasar discovery breaks distance record, constrains black hole formation models
events.one_liner: Astronomers led by Julien Wolf at the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy discovered the most distant quasar to date using ESA's Euclid space telescope. The quasar, designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed 'Dún Aonghasa' by the team, has a redshift of z = 8.13, placing it 630 million years after the Big Bang—40 million years earlier than the previous record holder and the first quasar with redshift greater than eight. Initial observations came from the Euclid Wide Survey, with confirmation provided by the W.M. Keck Observatory, Hubble Space Telescope, Large Binocular Telescope, and James Webb Space Telescope. The quasar contains a supermassive black hole that already existed at this early cosmic epoch. The discovery supports the scenario in which supermassive black holes form through direct collapse of large gas clouds and subsequently accumulate additional matter, constraining early black hole formation models.

events.title: COP31 Negotiations Collapse Without Climate Agreement
events.one_liner: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) collapsed on November 23, 2026, in Antalya, Türkiye, without adopting an overarching political agreement after nearly 200 nations failed to reach consensus. The impasse ended the longest UN climate summit on record after more than 49 hours of overtime negotiations, marking the first failure to formally adopt a political pact since the 2009 Copenhagen climate conference (COP15). COP31 President Murat Kurum ruled the proposed final text could not be adopted after the European Union, the United Kingdom, Norway, and Panama rejected draft language omitting any reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels. Major oil-producing states, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, opposed naming fossil fuels in the pact. Developing nations such as Kenya and Ghana criticized inadequate financial support and the removal of a proposed $120 billion adaptation finance target. The United States sent no official delegation for the second consecutive year following its withdrawal from the Paris Agreement. UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated in an official statement that while there is no consensus in the negotiating room, there is no ambiguity in the science, and every delay makes the climate task harder and more costly. Despite the collapse of the overarching political pact, parties still adopted technical decisions advancing a just transition framework, climate finance, and adaptation. Voluntary initiatives included pledges from 150 countries backing a target of 35 percent global electrification by 2035. The 2023 UAE Consensus from COP28, which calls on nations to transition away from fossil fuels, remains in effect. Parties will reconvene at COP32 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, next year to resume negotiations.

events.title: Extreme Wildfire Spread Accelerates Forest Ecosystem Change in North America
events.one_liner: A study published in Science Advances examined nearly 3,500 wildfires across western North American conifer forests between 2012 and 2023, analyzing more than 33,000 daily wildfire spread events. The research, led by Jonathan Coop at Western Colorado University and including Camille Stevens-Rumann of Colorado State University, found that fast-moving wildfires burn not only larger areas but also more severely. As fire spread rates increase, the amount of forest experiencing near-total tree mortality rises, along with the distance to surviving trees capable of reseeding burned areas. This leaves fewer surviving trees to naturally repopulate burned landscapes. The findings suggest that forests may increasingly be pushed toward long-term ecological change rather than recovery, potentially transitioning to shrublands, grasslands, or other vegetation better suited to warmer, drier conditions rather than recovering as forests. Climate change is intensifying these conditions: vapor pressure deficit (VPD) across the western U.S. between 1979 and 2020 increased primarily due to human-caused global warming, with the region passing a critical threshold around 2000. A 2016 study found that human-caused climate change caused over half of documented increases in fuel aridity since the 1970s and doubled cumulative forest fire area since 1984. In Canada, 2023 was the worst wildfire season on record, with approximately 15 million hectares burned—more than seven times the average of the preceding 10 years. The 2024 Smokehouse Creek Fire in Texas burned over one million acres, and the 2021 Dixie Fire in California burned nearly one million acres.

The 2025 L.A. fires affected highly urbanized, socio-demographically diverse communities with estimated costs of $76–131 billion USD. events.title: NASA's Voyager 1 probe reaches one light-day distance from Earth
events.one_liner: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a distance of one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026, at 2:16 a.m. PST, marking approximately 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometres) from Earth after 49 years in space since its 1977 launch. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours at approximately 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometres) per second. At this distance, radio signals from Voyager 1 now take approximately 24 hours to reach Earth, creating a nearly two-day round-trip communication delay between the spacecraft and mission control. Voyager 1 is the first human-made spacecraft to reach this distance. Originally launched in 1977 alongside its twin Voyager 2 to explore the outer planets, Voyager 1 visited Jupiter and Saturn before becoming the first human-made spacecraft to leave the heliosphere and enter interstellar space in 2012. Voyager 2 followed into interstellar space in 2018. The aging spacecraft continues to communicate with Earth despite its declining power supply; both Voyager spacecraft lose approximately four watts of power annually and rely on radioisotope power generators that produce electricity from decaying plutonium. Engineers have implemented energy-saving measures to maintain operations.
